1.line: Two paths: the person who delights in Torah, like a tree by water, and the wicked, like chaff in the wind.

2.line: The nations plot against Hashem and His anointed king; Hashem laughs at them, and calls on them to serve Him in awe.

3.line: David, fleeing from his son Avshalom: so many rise against me, yet I lie down and sleep, for Hashem protects me.

4.line: David asks to be answered, tells people to reflect quietly on their beds, and ends at peace: I lie down and sleep.

5.line: A morning prayer: hear my words, keep me from the deceitful, and through Your kindness I will come into Your House.

6.line: David, sick and weary, begs not to be punished in anger; by the end he knows Hashem has heard his weeping.

7.line: David, slandered by Kush of Binyamin: I am innocent; let the wicked fall into the pit they dug.

8.line: How majestic is Your Name: beside the heavens man is small, yet You crowned him and gave him rule over creation.

9.line: Thanks for Hashem's wonders and His judgment of the nations; He never forsakes those who seek Him.

10.line: Why do You stand far off? The wicked hunt the poor and think You don't see; rise up and help the helpless.

11.line: Told to flee like a bird to the mountains, David answers: I trust in Hashem, who sees everything from His throne.

12.line: Faithful people are disappearing and lips speak falsehood; Hashem's words are pure, refined like silver.

13.line: "How long will You forget me?" Four times David asks, then ends trusting and singing.

14.line: The fool says in his heart there is no G-d; all have gone astray. May Israel's salvation come from Tziyon.

15.line: Who may dwell on Your holy mountain? One who walks with integrity, speaks truth, keeps his word and takes no bribe.

16.line: I have no good apart from You: a pleasant portion, a path of life, and fullness of joy in Your presence.
16.known: Verse 8: "I have set Hashem before me always"

17.line: David asks to be judged fairly: guard me like the apple of the eye, hide me in the shadow of Your wings.

18.line: David's song on the day Hashem saved him from all his enemies and from Shaul: Hashem, my rock and my fortress.
18.known: Also the Haftorah of the seventh day of Pesach

19.line: The heavens tell the glory of G-d, and the Torah of Hashem is perfect, restoring the soul.
19.known: Said on Shabbos and Yom Tov in Pesukei Dezimra

20.line: "May Hashem answer you on the day of trouble": a prayer for the king going out to battle.
20.known: Said every weekday morning after Ashrei

21.line: The king rejoices in Hashem's strength; He gave him what his heart desired.

22.line: "My G-d, my G-d, why have You forsaken me?" From deep distress to praise in the great congregation.
22.known: The Sages read it as Esther's prayer

23.line: Hashem is my shepherd, I lack nothing; even in the valley of the shadow of death I fear no harm.

24.line: The earth is Hashem's; who may go up His mountain? Lift up your heads, O gates, and the King of glory will come in.

25.line: An alphabet prayer: teach me Your ways, forgive my sins, guard my soul.

26.line: Judge me, Hashem: I walked in integrity, kept away from the wicked, and I love the place of Your House.

27.line: Hashem is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? One thing I ask: to dwell in His House all my days.
27.known: Said from Rosh Chodesh Elul to Hoshana Rabbah

28.line: Do not be silent to me, and do not drag me off with the wicked. Save Your people and bless Your heritage.

29.line: Hashem's voice over the waters, breaking cedars and shaking the desert; He gives His people strength and peace.

30.line: A song for the dedication of the House: You lifted me up; weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.
30.known: Said every morning before Baruch She'amar

31.line: In You I take refuge; into Your hand I entrust my spirit. Be strong, all who hope in Hashem.
31.known: Verse 6 is said in the bedtime Shema

32.line: Fortunate is one whose sin is forgiven: while I kept silent I suffered; when I confessed, You forgave.

33.line: Sing a new song: by Hashem's word the heavens were made, and His plans stand forever.
33.known: Said on Shabbos and Yom Tov in Pesukei Dezimra

34.line: David, after pretending madness before Avimelech: I will bless Hashem at all times. Who desires life? Guard your tongue.
34.known: Said on Shabbos and Yom Tov in Pesukei Dezimra

35.line: A plea against those who repay good with evil and rejoice when David stumbles: fight those who fight me.

36.line: The wicked has no fear of G-d; Your kindness reaches the heavens. With You is the source of life; in Your light we see light.

37.line: Do not envy evildoers; trust Hashem and do good. An alphabet of teaching: the humble will inherit the land.
37.known: Verse 25 is said in Birkas Hamazon

38.line: David in sickness and pain, with friends standing far off: do not forsake me, hurry to help me.

39.line: I guarded my tongue, but my pain grew: let me know my end and how fleeting I am. Hear my prayer.

40.line: I hoped and hoped for Hashem; He lifted me from the pit and put a new song in my mouth.

41.line: Fortunate is one who cares for the poor. David, sick and betrayed even by a close friend, trusts Hashem. The end of the first book of Tehillim.

42.line: By the sons of Korach: like a deer longing for streams, my soul thirsts for G-d. Why are you downcast, my soul? Hope in G-d.

43.line: Continuing the last kapitel: send Your light and truth to lead me to Your holy mountain and Your altar.

44.line: We heard what You did for our fathers, yet now we are shamed and scattered. Wake up, and redeem us for Your kindness.

45.line: A song for the king: his majesty and justice, and the queen beside him in gold.

46.line: G-d is our refuge and strength: we will not fear though the earth shakes. Be still, and know that I am G-d.

47.line: Clap your hands, all peoples: G-d has gone up with a shout, Hashem with the sound of the shofar.
47.known: Said seven times before the shofar on Rosh Hashanah

48.line: Great is Hashem in the city of our G-d; kings saw it and fled in fear. Walk around Tziyon and count its towers.

49.line: Hear this, all peoples: wealth cannot redeem a life; a man in honor without understanding is like the beasts.
49.known: Said in a house of mourning

50.line: By Asaf: G-d summons the earth to judgment. He does not need offerings; He wants thanks and an upright way.

51.line: David, after Nasan the prophet rebuked him over Bas-Sheva: wash me, create in me a pure heart, a broken heart You will not despise.

52.line: After Doeg the Edomi informed on David to Shaul: the boaster with a lying tongue will be uprooted; I am like an olive tree in G-d's House.

53.line: The fool says in his heart there is no G-d (much like kapitel 14). May Israel's salvation come from Tziyon.

54.line: When the people of Zif told Shaul where David was hiding: save me by Your Name; He rescued me from every trouble.

55.line: Betrayed by a close friend he walked with to G-d's House: if only I had wings like a dove. Cast your burden on Hashem.

56.line: When the Plishtim seized David in Gas: when I am afraid I trust in You; You keep count of my tears.

57.line: When David fled from Shaul into the cave: in the shadow of Your wings I take refuge until the danger passes. I will wake the dawn.

58.line: To corrupt judges: you speak of justice but plan wrong. In the end people will say, there is a reward for the righteous.

59.line: When Shaul's men watched David's house to kill him: save me from my enemies; G-d is my fortress.

60.line: After victories over Aram and Edom, following a time of defeat: give us help against the enemy, for human help is worthless.

61.line: From the end of the earth I call: lead me to the rock too high for me. Add days to the king's life.

62.line: My soul waits in silence for G-d alone; He is my rock and my salvation. Trust in Him at all times.

63.line: In the desert of Yehudah: my soul thirsts for You in a dry land; I think of You on my bed through the night.

64.line: Hear my voice: the wicked plot in secret and sharpen their tongues like swords, but G-d's arrow strikes them.

65.line: Praise awaits You in Tziyon: You calm the seas and water the earth, and the fields are dressed in grain.

66.line: Shout to G-d, all the earth: He turned the sea into dry land. We went through fire and water, and He brought us out.

67.line: May G-d be gracious to us and bless us, so all the nations know His ways; the earth has given its produce.

68.line: Let G-d arise and His enemies scatter: father of orphans, He leads His people through the desert and gave the Torah at Sinai.

69.line: Save me, the waters have reached my soul: shamed for Your sake, I pray at a time of favor.

70.line: A short urgent plea: hurry to save me. I am poor and needy; do not delay.

71.line: In You I take refuge from my youth: do not cast me off in old age, when my strength fails.
71.known: Verse 9 is said in Selichos and on Yom Kippur

72.line: For Shlomo: may the king judge the poor with justice and rule from sea to sea. The prayers of David son of Yishai are ended.

73.line: By Asaf, opening the third book: I envied the wicked who prosper, until I came to G-d's sanctuary and understood their end. As for me, nearness to G-d is my good.

74.line: Why have You cast us off forever? The enemy has burned Your sanctuary. Remember Your people, and rise up for Your cause.

75.line: We thank You: when I choose the time, I will judge with fairness. G-d lowers one and raises another.

76.line: G-d is known in Yehudah; at His rebuke the enemy's chariots and horses fell asleep.

77.line: In my day of trouble I cried out and could not be comforted; then I remembered Your wonders of old, when You led Your people through the sea.

78.line: Asaf's long lesson from history: the wonders in Egypt and the desert, the people's forgetting, and G-d choosing Yehudah and David to shepherd them.

79.line: A lament after the Beis Hamikdash is destroyed: help us for the sake of Your Name.
79.known: Verses 6–7 are said at the Seder

80.line: Shepherd of Israel: Israel is a vine You brought out of Egypt, now trampled. The refrain asks three times: restore us.

81.line: Blow the shofar at the new moon: Rosh Hashanah, and G-d's plea, if only My people would listen to Me.

82.line: G-d stands among the judges and demands justice for the poor and the orphan.

83.line: Do not be silent, G-d: the nations plot together against Your people. Do to them as You did to Midyan and Sisera.

84.line: How beloved are Your dwellings: one day in Your courtyards is better than a thousand elsewhere.

85.line: You favored Your land and forgave Your people: kindness and truth meet, justice and peace kiss.

86.line: A prayer of David: I am poor and needy; teach me Your way, unite my heart to fear Your Name.

87.line: Hashem loves the gates of Tziyon; of Tziyon it will be said, every person was born there.

88.line: The darkest kapitel: from the depths, near death and abandoned by friends, the poet still calls to G-d every day.

89.line: Hashem's kindness and His promise to David's house forever, then the cry that it seems broken. The end of the third book.

90.line: A prayer of Moshe, opening the fourth book: a thousand years are like yesterday to You; teach us to count our days.
90.known: Said on Shabbos and Yom Tov in Pesukei Dezimra

91.line: One who dwells in the shelter of the Most High: you will not fear the terror of night; He will command His angels to guard you.
91.known: Said on Shabbos in Pesukei Dezimra and in the bedtime Shema

92.line: A song for the day of Shabbos: it is good to thank Hashem; the righteous will flourish like a palm tree.

93.line: Hashem reigns, robed in majesty; the floods raise their voice, but He is mightier.

94.line: G-d of retribution, appear: the wicked say Hashem does not see. Fortunate is the one You teach from Your Torah.

95.line: Come, let us sing to Hashem; do not harden your hearts as in the desert.

96.line: Sing a new song, all the earth: let the heavens rejoice and the trees sing, for He comes to judge the world.

97.line: Hashem reigns, let the earth rejoice: light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright.

98.line: Sing a new song, for He has done wonders: with trumpets and shofar, let the rivers clap their hands.

99.line: Hashem reigns, enthroned on the Keruvim: Moshe, Aharon and Shmuel called to Him, and He answered. He is holy.

100.line: A song of thanks: serve Hashem with joy; we are His people and the flock He tends.
100.known: Said on weekdays in Pesukei Dezimra

101.line: David's pledge as king: I will walk with integrity in my house, and keep slanderers and liars far from me.

102.line: A prayer of the afflicted: my days fade like a shadow, but You remain forever. Have mercy on Tziyon, for the time has come.

103.line: Bless Hashem, my soul, and forget none of His kindnesses: as far as east is from west, He removes our sins from us.

104.line: Bless Hashem, my soul: the whole of creation in order, the light, the seas, the springs, the animals; how many are Your works.

105.line: Give thanks and tell His wonders: the promise to the Avos, Yosef in Egypt, the plagues, and the Exodus.
105.known: Its first verses match Hodu, said every morning

106.line: The people's failings from Egypt through the desert and in the land, and Hashem's mercy each time. The end of the fourth book.

107.line: Opening the fifth book: travelers in the desert, prisoners, the sick and seafarers cry out, and Hashem saves them; let them give thanks.

108.line: My heart is ready, I will sing and wake the dawn; with G-d we will do valiantly (built from kapitlach 57 and 60).

109.line: Against accusers who repay love with hatred: let them curse, but You bless; He stands at the right hand of the poor.

110.line: Hashem says to my master: sit at My right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.

111.line: An alphabet of praise: His works are great, He gives food to those who fear Him, and the fear of Hashem is the beginning of wisdom.

112.line: An alphabet: fortunate is one who fears Hashem; he gives generously, his heart is steady, and his righteousness lasts forever.

113.line: Praise, servants of Hashem: He is high above the nations, yet lifts the poor from the dust.

114.line: When Israel left Egypt: the sea saw and fled, the Yarden turned back, and the mountains skipped like rams.

115.line: Not for us, but for Your Name: idols have mouths and cannot speak; Israel, trust in Hashem.

116.line: I love that Hashem hears my voice: He saved me from death. What can I give back? I will lift the cup of salvation.

117.line: The shortest kapitel, two verses: praise Hashem, all nations, for His kindness to us is great.

118.line: Give thanks, for His kindness is forever: from distress I called; the stone the builders rejected became the cornerstone.

119.line: The longest kapitel: 176 verses, eight for each letter of the Alef-Beis, all on love of the Torah and its mitzvos.
119.known: Verses spelling a name are said for someone who passed away

120.line: The first Song of Ascents: save me from lying lips; I am for peace, but they are for war.

121.line: I lift my eyes to the mountains: my help comes from Hashem; the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.

122.line: I rejoiced when they said, let us go to Hashem's House: pray for the peace of Yerushalayim.

123.line: Like servants watching their master's hand, our eyes look to Hashem: be gracious to us, we have had our fill of scorn.

124.line: Had Hashem not been with us when people rose against us, the waters would have swept us away. The snare broke and we escaped.

125.line: Those who trust in Hashem are like Mount Tziyon; as mountains surround Yerushalayim, Hashem surrounds His people.

126.line: When Hashem returns us to Tziyon we will be like dreamers; those who sow in tears will reap in joy.
126.known: Said before Birkas Hamazon on Shabbos and Yom Tov

127.line: For Shlomo: unless Hashem builds the house, its builders labor in vain. Children are a gift from Hashem.

128.line: Fortunate is everyone who fears Hashem: your wife like a fruitful vine, your children like olive shoots around your table.

129.line: Much have they afflicted me from my youth, but they have not overcome me.

130.line: From the depths I call You: with You is forgiveness; my soul waits for Hashem more than watchmen for the morning.
130.known: Said in the Ten Days of Teshuvah

131.line: My heart is not proud: I have quieted my soul like a weaned child with its mother.

132.line: Remember David, who would not rest until he found a place for Hashem; Hashem chose Tziyon as His home forever.

133.line: How good and pleasant when brothers sit together: like the oil on Aharon's beard, like the dew of Chermon.

134.line: The last Song of Ascents: servants of Hashem who stand in His House at night, lift your hands and bless Hashem.

135.line: Praise Hashem, who chose Yaakov: He struck Egypt and the kings of Canaan; idols are silver and gold.
135.known: Said on Shabbos and Yom Tov in Pesukei Dezimra

136.line: The Great Hallel: each verse of creation and the Exodus ends with "for His kindness is forever."
136.known: Said on Shabbos and Yom Tov, and at the Seder

137.line: By the rivers of Bavel we sat and wept: if I forget you, Yerushalayim, let my right hand forget its skill.
137.known: Said before Birkas Hamazon on weekdays

138.line: I thank You with all my heart: on the day I called, You answered me. Hashem will complete what is for me.

139.line: You know me completely: where can I go from Your spirit? You formed me in my mother's womb.

140.line: Save me from the violent man whose tongue is like a snake's; You shield my head on the day of battle.

141.line: Let my prayer be like incense before You: set a guard over my mouth.

142.line: A prayer of David in the cave: I look around and no one knows me; You are my refuge.

143.line: Hear my prayer and do not judge Your servant; teach me to do Your will, let Your good spirit lead me.

144.line: Blessed is Hashem, my rock, who trains my hands for battle: what is man, that You know him? Fortunate is the people whose G-d is Hashem.

145.line: An alphabet of praise: Hashem is good to all, near to all who call Him; You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing.
145.known: Ashrei, said three times a day

146.line: Do not trust in princes: Hashem keeps faith forever, frees prisoners, opens the eyes of the blind.
146.known: Said every morning in Pesukei Dezimra

147.line: Hashem rebuilds Yerushalayim and heals the brokenhearted; He counts the stars and gives His word to Yaakov.
147.known: Said every morning in Pesukei Dezimra

148.line: Praise Hashem from the heavens and from the earth: angels, sun and moon, fire and snow, kings and children.
148.known: Said every morning in Pesukei Dezimra

149.line: Sing a new song in the congregation of the pious: let Israel rejoice in its Maker.
149.known: Said every morning in Pesukei Dezimra

150.line: The end of Tehillim: praise Him with shofar, harp and dance; let every soul praise Hashem.
150.known: Said every morning in Pesukei Dezimra
